items.description: Sec. 4 (and Table A.5) give only 'a 20 × 60 finite-element grid'. Neither says which count runs horizontally or what shape the elements are. Sec. 5.1's 'full-span design that uses the complete horizontal domain' and the Top88 half-MBB convention (nely × nelx) point to 60 wide × 20 tall with square elements, but the text never states this.
readings: 60 elements horizontal × 20 vertical (nelx = 60, nely = 20), unit square elements; supported left edge and loaded right edge are 20 elements tall
20 elements horizontal × 60 vertical (nelx = 20, nely = 60), unit square elements

items.entity: unit downward point load on the right edge (Fig. 5(c) shared case)
items.description: Sec. 5.1 says only 'the right-edge loading'. Sec. 4 says the loaded node is picked at random from the 'lower, upper, or right boundary region'. The node's height along the right edge, and which test sample this is, appear only in Fig. 5(c) (init/F channel). The word 'region' even allows a node slightly inside the edge.
readings: right-edge node 1/4 of the edge height below the top
right-edge node 3/4 of the edge height below the top

items.description: Sec. 4 applies the unit load to 'a randomly selected admissible node'. Sec. 2.2 (Eq. 5) says the load channel F is 'nonzero at the loaded element, zero elsewhere'. If the location is read from the element-based channel, it is unclear which node or nodes of that element carry the load.
readings: unit point load on a single right-edge node
unit load on the upper right-side node of the marked element
unit load on the lower right-side node of the marked element
load split 0.5/0.5 between the two right-side nodes of the marked element

items.entity: target volume fraction of the Fig. 5(c) case
items.description: Sec. 4 draws each sample's target volume fraction uniformly from [0.3, 0.7]. Sec. 5.1 says the 'volume target' is the same in every Fig. 5(c) row but never gives the number. The 0.5 in Table A.5 belongs to the separate half-MBB check. Any value in [0.3, 0.7] is possible.

Sec. 2.1 says sensitivities are 'regularized via standard convolution filtering [3, 4]', which App. A.5 indicates is a sensitivity filter. No filter radius is given for the dataset or reference SIMP runs.
readings: rmin = 1.5 elements (Top88 default for a 60×20 mesh)

items.description: Sec. 2.1 cites 'optimality-criteria updates [31]' only. The move limit, damping exponent and bisection tolerance used to produce the SIMP reference are not given.

No convergence tolerance or iteration cap is given for the dataset's SIMP targets. Table A.5 belongs to a different half-MBB check. There the baseline converges at 94 iterations and the other runs stop at 100, which hints at a tolerance plus a 100-iteration cap. That cannot be assumed for the reference.
readings: stop when max|Δρ| < 0.01, no iteration cap (Top88)
max|Δρ| < 0.01 or 100 iterations, whichever comes first

items.entity: starting density field of the SIMP reference run
items.description: Sec. 4 stores a noisy ρ_init with each sample: the target volume fraction plus Gaussian-smoothed variation of amplitude 0.05, clipped to [0.001, 1]. Fig. 5(c) shows this 'shared init' beside the SIMP reference. Sec. 5.4 says re-runs differ from the 'reference (clean) run' only in the starting field. The text never says whether the dataset's SIMP target started from this ρ_init or from the standard uniform field. SIMP is non-convex, and Table 3 shows the start can change the result.
readings: uniform ρ = target volume fraction everywhere (Top88 start)
the case's clean ρ_init (volume fraction + smoothed noise, clipped to [0.001, 1]) shown in the Fig. 5(c) init column

items.entity: random perturbation defining the clean ρ_init
items.description: Sec. 4 gives only 'Gaussian-smoothed random variation with amplitude 0.05'. Missing: the smoothing length, the noise distribution, what 'amplitude' means (maximum or std), whether the field is re-centred on the volume target, and the RNG seed. Without these the Fig. 5(c) init cannot be regenerated, and the dataset is available only on request. This matters if the reference started from ρ_init.
readings: i.i.d. Gaussian field smoothed with σ = 2 elements, scaled to max|δ| = 0.05
smoothed field scaled to standard deviation 0.05

items.entity: solid Young's modulus E0 (and out-of-plane thickness)
items.description: Eq. 2 introduces the solid modulus E0 but gives no value. Thickness is not given either. Both only scale the absolute compliance C reported in the Fig. 5(c) panel titles.
readings: a physical modulus, e.g., E0 = 210 GPa, with a physical thickness

items.entity: near-void modulus Emin / density lower bound
items.description: Eq. 2 uses a near-void modulus Emin but gives no value. The 0.001 clip on ρ_init (Sec. 4) hints at a density floor, but the optimizer's density bounds are not stated. Emin also sets the void stiffness in the thresholded compliance evaluation.
readings: density floor ρ_min = 0.001 with E = ρ^3·E0 (99-line style)

items.description: No Poisson's ratio is given anywhere in the text.

items.entity: 2D constitutive assumption (plane stress vs. plane strain)
items.description: The text does not say whether the 2D analysis is plane stress or plane strain. The element formulation is not stated either: App. A.5 only mentions a 'Top88/SIMP optimizer', which implies bilinear Q4 plane-stress elements.

items.entity: compliance evaluation of the SIMP reference (thresholding)
items.description: Sec. 5.1, the Fig. 5(b)/(c) captions and Table 1 refer to 'thresholded' compliance, and the Fig. 5(c) panel titles give the absolute reference C (shown only in the figure). The threshold value is not stated. Nor is it stated whether the SIMP reference is binarized before computing C(ρ_SIMP; P) in Eq. 13. This does not change the optimized layout, but it changes the reported compliance in a design-dependent way.
readings: C of the continuous (gray-scale) final SIMP density
C after binarizing the SIMP design at ρ ≥ 0.5 (void = Emin)
C after binarizing by keeping the volfrac·N densest elements solid
